commit_message: [LinalgExt] Add affine quantization and dequantization ops (#24901) Adds `iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine` and `iree_linalg_ext.dequantize_affine` to represent QDQ directly in LinalgExt, preserving quantization parameters for subsequent compiler transformations. Independent indexing maps for the input, scale, zero point, and output express per-tensor, per-channel, and blockwise quantization. The ops support optional zero points, explicit storage and zero-point signedness, and arithmetic in the scale's element type. Quantization rounds ties to even and clamps to the specified storage range. Includes operation verification, shape reification, and decomposition into elementwise Linalg generics. Dispatch creation decomposes remaining QDQ ops before fusion, allowing earlier optimizations to consume the explicit quantization representation. Implements the QDQ operation layer of [Linalg(_ext) native QDQ #24862](https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24862). --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬 Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context)

commit_message:
[Runtime] Fix sysfs incorrect topology (#24828)

Fixes incorrect topology creation by using the `node/node<N>/cpulist` to
deduce the NUMA nodes and CPU relation instead of cluster or package ids
which have different meanings.
As far as I can tell, the node_id is intended to always be the NUMA node
id, since this is later used to bind memory to a specific NUMA node.

- Fixed cluster/numa node confusion
- Fixed ignored file read errors
- Fixed ignored path length errors
- Added a testing path injection
- Added tests

Fixes https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24761

Co-Authored-by: Claude (I had to rely on Claude a bit more than usual
for sysfs knowledge)

commit_message:
[Stream] Fix ARC double-dealloca of aliased control-flow results (#24841)

The ARC pass emitted multiple deallocations for possibly aliasing
results pointing to the same buffer, leading to double-deallocation
and/or deallocation/usage race.

ARC assumed that each result of a control-flow op is a distinct buffer,
unless the values yielded into two results resolve to the same buffer
through their tied-value chain. But a (nested) control-flow op's result
is defined by a control-flow op, which is not tied to anything, since it
may hold a different yielded value on each path. The analysis then
treated both as separate buffers.

The fix collects the tied-value chain for each path. A yielded value
thus resolves to the set of allocations it
may hold. If there is an overlap, the values may alias.


Think the pass might need a closer look/some refactoring at some point -
the fix is just patching this up.
